en: There's a TV drama called "Even Lotto Winners Go to Work."
Don't watch it. This isn't an ad.
I haven't seen it either.
An ordinary office worker
wins the lottery.
1.3 billion won.
Not 13 billion.
Too little to quit over,
too much to ignore.
So the winner keeps going to work.
But after the win,
work felt different.
Before, it was all about surviving,

text:
그 다음에 *인정*받아야 된다
내가 승진해야 된다
en: being recognized, getting promoted.
He staked his life on it.

text:
딴 사람이 잘
보이지 않았단 말이야
en: He couldn't really see anyone else.
But going in as a lottery winner,
he could breathe.
Getting fired would be fine, so he was at ease.
Fear loosened its grip on him.
Then he started to notice the junior staff.
"He's struggling. I should buy him lunch."
He sees his coworkers' troubles,

text:
그래서 이 친구가 좋은 *팀*을
만든다는 스토리래요
en: and ends up building a great team.
It's like that.
Why does the gospel turn us toward others?
Here's why:
God is with me in my life.
Only when you're sure your life won't fall apart

text:
그 삶에 *확신*이 있어야지
그것이 눈에 보인단 말이에요
en: do other people come into view.
It takes security to see them.
If just 1.3 billion won from the lottery
can turn a life toward others,

text:
온 천지를 창조하신 하나님이
우리의 *아버지*가 되시는데
en: and the God who made heaven and earth is our Father,

text:
왜 그렇게 *불안*과 두려움
가운데 살아가야 됩니까?
en: why live in such anxiety and fear?
